extraction.name: Geometry3K
extraction.description: A large-scale benchmark consisting of 3,002 SAT-style geometry problems collected from two high-school textbooks, covering diverse graph and goal types. Each problem is annotated with dense descriptions in formal language for symbolic reasoning and interpretable problem solving.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Ran Gong, Shibiao Jiang, Liang Qiu, Siyuan Huang, Xiaodan Liang, Song-Chun Zhu
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Groups of well-trained annotators with undergraduate degrees manually collected each problem with its problem text, geometry diagram, four candidate choices, and correct answer from two popular textbooks for high school students across grades 6-12 by two online digital libraries (McGraw-Hill and Geometryonline). Each problem was labeled with the corresponding problem goal and geometry shapes.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Geometry problems from two popular textbooks for high school students across grades 6-12, sourced from two online digital libraries (McGraw-Hill and Geometryonline). Each problem includes problem text, geometry diagram, four candidate choices, and correct answer.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Groups of well-trained annotators with undergraduate degrees manually collect each problem with its problem text, geometry diagram, four candidate choices, and correct answer. Each problem data is labeled with the corresponding problem goal and geometry shapes.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Rule-based text parsing and neural object detecting
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset contains limited problem types compared to the full scope of geometry problems. The predicates for problem text are more evenly distributed than those for diagrams, mainly because the problem text describes diverse geometric shapes, attributes, and relations while diagrams display the basic properties of points, lines, and arcs. Less than 1% of the problems in Geometry3K could be solved when the problem diagram is not provided.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for training and evaluating geometry problem solvers. The annotated formal language is used to train and evaluate problem parsers. The dataset is divided into train, validation, and test sets with the ratio of 0.7:0.1:0.2 for model development and evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset and evaluation baselines are publicly released. The project with code and data is available at https://lupantech.github.io/inter-gps.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Rule-based text parsing and neural object detection to convert problem text and diagrams into formal language
